messages.content:
Simulate a fictional lost-sales inventory system exactly. There is no stochastic prediction and no missing information beyond the explicit reporting cutoff.
Receipts add quantity to stock. Demands consume min(stock, quantity); any unmet quantity is lost (never backlogged). A stockout means strictly positive unmet demand, not merely ending with zero stock.
For raw report histories: first keep reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff. Then choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id. Revisions REPLACE earlier reports, not add to them. Then keep chosen events with event_time <= target_time. Apply these events in (event_time, event_id) order, starting from initial_stock. Ignore any report not visible at the knowledge cutoff even if its event occurred earlier. Arrival order is not event order.
The canonical arm supplies the already selected eligible events in event-time order. The snapshot arm supplies the exactly replayed historical state. These are explicitly identified, executable preprocessing interventions.
After the historical reconstruction, apply every event in the given future_schedule in (event_time, event_id) order from the reconstructed stock. This is an explicitly known hypothetical scenario, not privileged knowledge about a real future.
Return five integers through submit_answer: stock_at_target; total historical_lost through target_time using visible revisions; stock_at_horizon after the scenario; future_lost for the scenario ONLY; first_future_stockout_time, the earliest future scenario event time with unmet demand, or -1 if no future demand is unmet. Do not count historical stockouts in that last field.

We need to compute, given raw report histories and knowledge_cutoff of 100 (the same as target_time?), the visible revisions and events up to target_time (100). Then we need to apply these events in order (event_time, event_id) to reconstruct the state as of target_time (which is 100). Then we need to compute total historical_lost through target_time (i.e., sum of unmet demand for those events). Also compute stock_at_target (stock after processing events up to target_time, i.e., same as stock after all events with event_time <= target_time). Then we apply the future_schedule: we need to apply every future event from the scenario after the historical reconstruction, starting from the reconstructed stock after target_time? Actually after historical reconstruction but before future events, we have the stock at target_time. Then we apply future schedule events (event_time potentially beyond target_time) in order of (event_time, event_id). Since future schedule times are all >100? Actually they start at 101, 102, etc. The horizon_time is 130, which is presumably the final time we consider (target_time:100 horizon_time:130). We need to compute stock_at_horizon after applying all the future events up to horizon_time. Also compute future_lost: total lost demand for those future events. Also compute first_future_stockout_time: earliest event time (>=101) where unmet demand occurs (i.e., demand quantity > stock at that point). If no future demand unmet, return -1.

All events (historical, future) have known quantities. The "knowledge cutoff": only reports with received_time <= knowledge_cutoff are visible. So we need to filter out all reports with received_time > 100. But wait, knowledge_cutoff is 100, but many reports have received_time >100. They are not visible. So we only consider those with received_time <= 100. Then for each event_id (i.e., each reporting event) we need to keep the highest visible revision of that event.

Important: Even if a report (revision) is visible (received_time <= cutoff) and its event_time is before target_time, we need to apply the highest visible revision for each event_id. If a given event_id has multiple revisions visible, we only keep highest revision number (or highest revision? The spec: "choose the highest visible revision for EACH event_id". So for each event_id, we keep the report with highest revision (largest integer) among those with received_time <= cutoff. If no visible report for that event_id, we ignore it entirely. Then after picking highest visible revision per event_id, we keep only those events with event_time <= target_time. Then apply them sorted by (event_time, event_id). Note: event_id string can be compared lexicographically for tie-breaking? The spec says sort by (event_time, event_id) order; standard lexicographical sorting by event_time first, then event_id. So we need that ordering.
